beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: This model fish tank is a rectangular prism: a box shape. Its inside measures seven centimeters long, four wide, and six high.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Where did the cubes go? How can we find its volume?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Volume counts the unit cubes that fill the space, without gaps or overlaps. Each cube here has one-centimeter edges.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Start with the base, the bottom face. Seven squares along, and four rows. Twenty-eight square centimeters.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Give each square a cube one centimeter high. The same base holds twenty-eight cubes in one layer.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The tank is six centimeters high, so we need six of those layers. One, two, three, four, five, six.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Twenty-eight cubes in every layer, times six layers. One hundred sixty-eight cubic centimeters.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: So multiplying two edges finds one layer. The third edge tells how many layers!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Exactly. Adding the edge lengths only measures lengths. To count all the cubes, multiply.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Here, the letters mean volume, length, width, and height. We can also call the base area capital *B*. Volume is base area times height.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: What about this step-shaped solid? It is eight centimeters long and three deep. The tall end is six high; the low end is two.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Eight times three times six?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: That would fill the empty space above the low end, too. Instead, cut straight down at the step.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Separate the two boxes. Both are three centimeters deep. Each needs its own length and height.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The tall box is three by three by six. Its volume is fifty-four cubic centimeters.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The low box is only five long: eight minus three. Its height is two, not six.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Five times three times two gives thirty cubic centimeters.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Fit them back. Nothing is missing, and nothing is counted twice. Add their volumes: fifty-four plus thirty is eighty-four.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Could we cut across instead?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Yes. Cut level with the low part, then lift the top box.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The bottom slab uses the full length: eight times three times two. Forty-eight cubic centimeters.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The top box is only four high. Six minus the bottom two leaves four.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Three times three times four is thirty-six. Add forty-eight and thirty-six: eighty-four cubic centimeters again.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Different pieces, but the same amount of space!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Exactly. Either cut counts every part once. The solid never changed.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: This box holds sixty cubic centimeters. Its base is three by four. How tall is it?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: One layer holds twelve cubes.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: How many groups of twelve make sixty? Divide sixty by twelve. Five layers.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Each layer is one centimeter high, so the height is five centimeters. Check: three times four times five is sixty.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Divide by both known edges multiplied together. The same method works whichever edge is missing.

do.text: Missing edge = volume ÷ product of known edges.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Which three boxes hold eighteen cubic centimeters? Each caption gives three edge lengths in centimeters. Pause and multiply.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: *A*: two times nine times one is eighteen. *B*: three times three times two is eighteen.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: *C*: six times one times three is eighteen. *D*: three times three times three is twenty-seven.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: So *A*, *B*, and *C* hold the same volume, even though they look different.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Multiply all three edges. You can change the multiplication order: six times one times three equals six times three times one.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Two planters need soil filled to the top. These are their inside measurements, in feet.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The first needs four times two times three: twenty-four cubic feet.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The second needs two times two times two: eight cubic feet.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Add the two volumes. Thirty-two cubic feet of soil fills both.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Choose two boxes whose combined volume is greater than thirty and less than thirty-five cubic centimeters.

do.text: Choose a pair by its total

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: First multiply each box's three edges. The volumes here are twenty-four, eight, and twenty-seven.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Test pairs. *A* and *C* make fifty-one: too much. *B* and *C* make thirty-five, exactly the upper bound. We need less than thirty-five.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: *A* and *B* make thirty-two. That is greater than thirty and less than thirty-five. Choose both.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Neither box alone has to be in the range. Their total does!

do.text: Compare the sum with both bounds.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: For an exact total, multiply, add a pair, then check for equality.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One solid. A tall box and a low box.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Or a bottom slab and a top box. The same eighty-four cubic centimeters.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Base area times height. And when a solid is made of boxes, find each box's volume and add.
